title: One decision. A useful story.
pages: The decision is a starting point.
A product update tells buyers what changed. The reasoning helps them understand why it matters.
Name the buyer problem.
Explain the situation that made this decision necessary. Keep confidential details out.
Show the trade-off.
What did the team choose? What did it give up? State where the approach fits and where it does not.
Bring the evidence.
Use a permissioned demonstration, a source-linked observation or a clearly marked example. Do not substitute a claim for proof.
Explain the implication.
Give the buyer a useful question to ask when evaluating a similar approach.

title: Before a draft is ready.
pages: Check the material.
Did this experience happen? Is the product claim true today? Keep each answer linked to its source.
Check the permission.
Can the example be shared? Who owns the media? A public page is not automatic permission to reuse it.
Check the meaning.
Keep the qualification that makes the claim true. Edit for clarity without changing the evidence.
Give the founder the exact draft.
Approval applies to the wording and media being reviewed. Changed claims return for review.
Keep the next step clear.
Deliver approved text and artwork with sources, accessibility text and a clear publishing owner.
